sections.html:
Hoover is in north central Alabama and belongs to the Birmingham metro area. The city spans two counties, Jefferson and Shelby, so the first thing to confirm is which county holds your parcel. The answer tells you which probate office files your deed. Hoover uses ten different ZIP codes, so the mailing city on a tax bill or listing does not always tell you the county.

Downtown Birmingham is about 11 miles north by I-65 or US-31. Hoover was incorporated in 1967 and counted 688 people in 1970, 62,742 in 2000, 92,606 in 2020 and an estimated 93,550 in 2025. It is Alabama's sixth largest city, and growth has slowed to about one percent above the 2020 count.

The 2020 census found 39,008 housing units and 36,799 households, with 5.7 percent of units vacant. Homeowner vacancy was 1.3 percent and rental vacancy 9.6 percent. The median age was 39.2, with 17.2 percent of residents aged 65 or over. A house in an older neighborhood now competes with newer ones built during the boom years.

Hoover includes dozens of named communities, among them Bluff Park, Riverchase, Ross Bridge, Greystone, Inverness, Trace Crossings, Shoal Creek, Lake Cyrus and Shades Mountain. Each has its own age of housing and its own buyer pool, so a flat answer about what a Hoover house is worth rarely holds.

When you describe your house, name its community, give the year it was built and list what has been replaced. Riverchase was annexed on September 8, 1980, and the I-459 and I-65 interchange inside the city gave the area easy highway access, which still draws commuters.

The city's own school system runs ten elementary schools, three middle schools and two high schools: Hoover High School and Spain Park High School. Rezoning in 2018 changed which grades attend Brock's Gap Intermediate and Bumpus Middle, so a family looking at an older listing may ask which zone it falls into. The Shelby-Hoover campus of Jefferson State Community College is here, as is a Faulkner University campus on Valleydale Road.

Two interstates, I-65 and I-459, cross Hoover. U.S. 31 cuts through the middle from north to south, U.S. 280 serves the east side and State Route 150 runs east to west. Valleydale Road connects U.S. 31 with U.S. 280, and the Birmingham-Jefferson County Transit Authority runs buses into town.

The yearly bill falls due on October 1, and a balance still open after December 31 is delinquent. Sell in the fall and the two of you must settle that year's bill at the closing table, so ask the closing office how it will be divided.

sections.h2: Deed tax and where to record
sections.html:
Moving title triggers a state tax of 50 cents on every $500 of value (Alabama Code 40-22-1), and the deed must carry proof of the price actually paid. Payment comes first; the clerk will not accept the instrument for record until it is made.

For the Jefferson side, go to the probate court's Birmingham division at 716 North Richard Arrington Jr. Blvd. or its Bessemer division at 1801 3rd Avenue North. Both are open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. A copy of a recorded deed costs $1.00 per page in the record room. The clerks will not hunt for liens or write a deed, which is work for a lawyer or a title office.

Parcel locationWhere the deed is recorded
Jefferson County side of HooverJefferson County Probate Court, Birmingham or Bessemer division
Shelby County side of HooverShelby County probate office

Paying cash changes who funds the purchase, not the legal steps. Someone searches the title, a deed is drawn, the transfer tax is paid and the filing goes to the right county.

With no lender there is no appraisal, and that is a common source of delay gone. Liens, open tax bills and clouded title are still there to be cleared before the closing date.

  • Find out whether Jefferson or Shelby holds the parcel.
  • Have the title searched for liens.
  • Make sure this year's property tax is paid or prorated.
  • Decide between repairing first and selling as-is.

Because buyers sort by community, lead with the name of your neighborhood and the school zone, then the age and condition of the roof, the heating and cooling, and the kitchen. Houses built in the boom years may be reaching the age when roofs and air handlers need replacing, and buyers know it.

If you plan to sell as-is, say that up front and describe what is wrong. A cash buyer who sees the real condition can make a firm offer, and you avoid a drawn-out renegotiation after an inspection.

Owners who age in place, heirs who inherit a family house and people relocating for work are all common sellers here. Houses in those situations often carry deferred repairs, which is where a buyer who purchases as-is can fit. A job change or relocation can also force a quick sale.

No repair is required by law before listing. A title search and a current tax payment are still needed to close.

sections.h2: A timeline for a Hoover sale
sections.html:
A sale usually starts with a call or form to request an offer. The buyer looks at the house, you sign a contract, and the title search follows. If the search turns up a lien or a missing signature, that gets fixed before the closing date.

On closing day you sign the deed and the settlement papers. Any lender is paid off from the proceeds, the tax is split, and the deed is filed with the probate office of the county where the parcel sits. Proceeds usually reach you once the filing is complete.

A clean file moves in a matter of weeks. An estate, a missing owner or an old lien takes longer, so start gathering papers before you ask for an offer.

Take a photo ID, the deed or trust papers, a payoff letter from any lender, and all keys and garage openers. If more than one person owns the house, each owner signs. The title office will say if anything else is needed.

The settlement statement shows the sale price, any payoff, the tax split and your net. If the office can send it ahead, read it the day before and ask about any line that looks wrong.

sections.h2: Selling with a loan or tax owed
sections.html: An open mortgage or a late tax bill will not block a sale. Your lender states a payoff figure, it is paid out of your proceeds, and the lien lifts once the deed is filed. Get both numbers early so you know what you will keep.

faqs.q: Is Hoover in Jefferson County or Shelby County?
faqs.a: Both. Hoover spans Jefferson and Shelby Counties, so a parcel can be in either. Your tax bill or the county records will show which probate office files your deed.

faqs.q: What is the population of Hoover, Alabama?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 92,606 people, and the 2025 estimate is 93,550. Hoover is the sixth largest city in Alabama.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Hoover?
faqs.a: They fall due October 1 and are delinquent once December 31 passes.

faqs.q: How much is the Alabama deed tax on a sale?
faqs.a: The charge is 50 cents per $500 of value, or part of $500, set by Alabama Code 40-22-1, and the deed needs proof of the price paid.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Hoover house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Homes with deferred repairs sell to buyers who purchase as-is, and no repairs are required by law before listing. A title search and an up to date tax payment are still needed to close.
